hint: diagram: query-key-value flow through softmax and weighted sum
pdfExcerpt: We compute attention as a weighted sum of values, where the weight assigned to each value is computed by a compatibility function of the query with the corresponding key. In practice we compute attention on a set of queries simultaneously, packed into a matrix Q. The keys and values are also packed into matrices K and V. Attention(Q,K,V) = softmax(QK^T / sqrt(d_k)) V.

hint: diagram: flow showing how a BF16 value splits into sign, exponent, mantissa and is reconstructed
pdfExcerpt: BFloat16 (BF16) is a 16-bit floating-point format with 1 sign bit, 8 exponent bits, and 7 mantissa bits. Decomposition extracts these three components from a 32-bit FP32 representation. Reconstruction reassembles them back into FP32 by zero-padding the mantissa.

hint: diagram: expander graph with edge-expansion cuts, contrasted with a fat-tree hierarchy
pdfExcerpt: Expander graphs provide near-optimal bisection bandwidth with far fewer links than a fat tree. Edge expansion h(G) measures the minimum ratio of the boundary of a vertex subset to its size. Random regular graphs achieve high expansion with high probability, making them attractive as datacenter network topologies.

hint: diagram: request flow through tokenizer, cache lookup, model, and response
pdfExcerpt: The system caches intermediate key-value states keyed by prompt prefix hash. On a cache hit, the stored state is reused, skipping recomputation of the shared prefix. On a miss, the full forward pass runs and the result is stored for future reuse.

hint: diagram: state machine for follower, candidate, and leader transitions
pdfExcerpt: Each server is in one of three states: follower, candidate, or leader. A follower that receives no communication converts to a candidate and starts an election. If it receives votes from a majority, it becomes leader. If another server establishes itself as leader, the candidate reverts to follower.

hint: chart: quantization error decreasing as bit width increases from 2 to 16 bits
pdfExcerpt: We measure mean-squared quantization error across bit widths from 2 to 16 bits on a held-out weight distribution. Error decreases roughly exponentially with bit width, with diminishing returns beyond 8 bits for this model family.

topic: Throughput vs batch size for the serving system
hint: chart: request throughput scaling with batch size before saturating
pdfExcerpt: We sweep batch size from 1 to 256 and measure sustained throughput on an A100 GPU. Throughput scales roughly linearly with batch size until the KV cache exceeds available memory, at which point it plateaus.

hint: chart: p99 latency increasing with sequence length
pdfExcerpt: We report p50, p95, and p99 latency for sequence lengths from 128 to 8192 tokens. Tail latency grows superlinearly past 4096 tokens due to quadratic attention cost, motivating the sparse attention variant proposed in Section 4.

hint: table: rows for cost, throughput, cabling complexity across fat-tree, dragonfly, and expander topologies
pdfExcerpt: We compare three datacenter network topologies — fat-tree, dragonfly, and random expander — along the axes of bisection bandwidth, cabling cost, and fault tolerance under random link failures.

hint: table: rows for each ablated component with the resulting accuracy drop
pdfExcerpt: We ablate each of the four proposed components in turn — the gating mechanism, the auxiliary loss, the warm-start schedule, and the sparse routing — and report the resulting drop in validation accuracy for each.

hint: math: definition of edge expansion and its relation to the spectral gap
pdfExcerpt: Edge expansion is the core property analyzed in this section. For a d-regular graph G, the Cheeger inequality relates the edge expansion h(G) to the second eigenvalue of the normalized adjacency matrix.

hint: math: derivation of the O(n^2) time and memory complexity of full self-attention
pdfExcerpt: Standard self-attention computes an n-by-n attention matrix, requiring O(n^2 d) time and O(n^2) memory for sequence length n and hidden dimension d. This quadratic scaling motivates the sparse and linear attention variants surveyed here.

topic: Convergence bound for stochastic gradient descent
hint: math: convergence rate bound in terms of step size and variance
pdfExcerpt: Under a bounded-variance assumption on the stochastic gradient, standard SGD analysis gives a convergence rate that depends on both the step size and the gradient variance, with the optimal step size shrinking as the variance grows.

hint: diagram: router dispatching tokens to a subset of expert feed-forward networks
pdfExcerpt: Each token is routed by a learned gating function to the top-k experts among N feed-forward expert networks. Only the selected experts are activated for that token, keeping the per-token compute roughly constant as N grows.

hint: diagram: micro-batches flowing through sequential pipeline stages with forward and backward passes
pdfExcerpt: The model is partitioned into sequential stages assigned to different devices. Micro-batches are streamed through the pipeline so that multiple stages are active concurrently, reducing the idle 'bubble' time compared to naive sequential execution.

hint: diagram: mindmap of the paper's contributions — a new cache eviction policy, a compression scheme, and an evaluation framework
pdfExcerpt: This paper makes three contributions: a recency-aware KV-cache eviction policy, a low-rank compression scheme for retained entries, and an evaluation framework comparing both against five baseline systems across three model families.
